candidate.inputs: finite ordered list of DISTINCT opaque argument identities A, finite set of directed attacks (attacker, target), all endpoints must be in A; no inferred edges or probabilistic weights
candidate.result: triple (IN, OUT, UNDEC), each a disjoint list of argument IDs in ORIGINAL input order and a total partition of A, with no argument unclassified
candidate.law: Grounded Dung characteristic F(S) = {a | every attacker b of a is attacked by some c in S}. Iterate from empty S to least fixed point G. IN=G, OUT={b | exists a in G with attack(a,b)}, UNDEC=A\(IN∪OUT). Edges are directed. A self-attacking or unbroken mutual attack remains UNDEC in the absence of externally grounded attackers. Empty A returns three empty lists.

witnesses.why: external grounded d defeats a; then b reinstated
unrelated accepted argument cannot resolve mutual attack
finite empty domain has empty fixed point

falsifiers: A↔B with no outside attackers cannot arbitrarily accept A or B; both UNDEC.
Under a→b→c, returning c=UNDEC instead of IN violates defended iteration.
Treating edges as undirected reverses attack/defence and violates the witness for one-way chains.
IN/OUT/UNDEC overlap or omit an argument violates total-partition invariant.
Returning every proposition not proved true as OUT violates grounded undecidability.
Using a third truth bit or changing D1 YES/NO or D2 source structure violates binary-language architecture.
Duplicated node identities, unknown attack endpoints and malformed edges must reject instead of silently inventing nodes.
Calling model output a truthful fact about the world without validated attack/evidence sources violates observation boundary.
